title: Why do sides and corners give the same numbers?
description: The sides and the corners of the regular polygons are counted, and both give the same number sequence. Each corner is a place where two sides meet, so a closed shape has as many corners as sides.
teaching_notes: One idea: count the sides, count the corners, and see that going round a closed shape gives one corner after every side. Watch for students who count the corner at the start twice.

source: Figure it Out Q1 (Try This), p.11
video_script.why: The child counts the sides and the corners of the regular polygons, as in the solved example, and explains why the two counts are the same.

final_answer.spoken: the counting numbers starting at three

maths_rules: corners of the regular polygons: 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, the same sequence
each corner is where two sides meet, so a closed shape has as many corners as sides
check: a square has 4 sides, 4 x 2 = 8 side ends, each corner holds 2 side ends, 8 / 2 = 4 corners
